Definition: from G251; a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher:--fisher(-man).
BiblicalUsage: halieús is a plain word for fisher(-man). In Matthew 4:18, the text says "for they were fishers." In Matthew 4:19, the text says "and I will make you fishers of men."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, halieús is a reminder that the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
